fields.Name: Eventbrite
fields.Description: Eventbrite connector — syncs organizations, events, ticket classes, attendees, orders, questions, discounts, venues, webhooks, categories, and formats via the Eventbrite REST API v3 (OAuth2 / personal-token Bearer auth).

Configuration.AuthFlowNotes: Two paths: (1) Private token — issued from the Eventbrite account API Keys page, used as a long-lived Bearer token for single-org integrations. (2) OAuth2 authorization-code flow for app partners acting on behalf of multiple users. Authorization URL: https://www.eventbrite.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=YOUR_API_KEY&redirect_uri=YOUR_REDIRECT_URI. Token URL: POST https://www.eventbrite.com/oauth/token (grant_type=authorization_code; body params: client_id, client_secret, code, redirect_uri). Both flows produce a private token/access token used as Authorization: Bearer <token>. The connector credential holds the resolved token; the grant-type path is the AuthFlow shape here.
Configuration.TokenRefreshStrategyNotes: Private tokens do not expire. OAuth2 access tokens (from the authorization-code flow) also do not have a documented expiry / refresh-token mechanism in the v3 API spec. Vendor docs describe only an initial token exchange; no refresh token endpoint is documented. Token must be re-obtained by re-running the authorization-code flow.
Configuration.APIVersioningStrategyNotes: Version is embedded in the URL path as /v3/ (e.g. https://www.eventbriteapi.com/v3/events/). No version header or accept-header versioning. The apiary.io spec is tagged as Eventbrite API v3; no other public major versions are currently documented.

PaginationDefaults.notes: All paginated endpoints return a pagination envelope with fields: continuation (opaque cursor token), has_more_items (boolean), page_number (integer), page_count (integer), page_size (integer), object_count (total records). To advance: verify has_more_items is true, copy continuation token, reissue the same request with ?continuation=<token>. When all records have been retrieved the continuation token is present but the next call returns an empty list. Error BAD_CONTINUATION_TOKEN (HTTP 400) is returned on invalid tokens. No page_size override documented in the spec.

IncrementalSyncCapability.notes: Two object families support the changed_since query parameter: (1) Attendees — GET /events/{event_id}/attendees/ accepts changed_since (ISO 8601 datetime) to filter attendees changed on or after the specified time, and last_item_seen (used in conjunction with changed_since to page incremental batches without duplication). (2) Orders — GET /organizations/{org_id}/orders/ accepts changed_since (ISO 8601); GET /events/{event_id}/orders/ accepts changed_since AND last_item_seen. No other objects expose a changed_since or equivalent incremental filter in the v3 spec. Events, Venues, Questions, TicketClasses, Discounts, etc. require full re-fetch or content-hash comparison for incremental sync.

Configuration.WebhooksNotes: Webhook subscriptions managed via POST /organizations/{org_id}/webhooks/ (create), GET /organizations/{org_id}/webhooks/ (list), DELETE /webhooks/{webhook_id}/ (delete). Webhook actions (event types) set at creation via comma-separated actions field: event.created, event.published, order.placed, and others. Webhook delivery payload (the inbound HTTP POST to the registered endpoint_url) is out of scope — it is a push signal, not a pull sync stream. Webhook subscription management is in scope.
Configuration.WebhooksSignatureAlgorithmNotes: No HMAC signature algorithm is documented for webhook delivery payloads in the v3 spec. The webhook payload verification method is not documented in the apiary spec reviewed (last updated 2024-02-16).
Configuration.BulkOperationsNotes: No batch or bulk endpoints are present in the Eventbrite API v3 spec. All read and write operations are single-record or paginated-list endpoints. GET list endpoints with pagination are not bulk-write operations.

universalPK.notes: The Eventbrite API v3 uses id as the universal PK field name across all core resource types (Event, Order, Attendee, TicketClass, Organization, Venue, Discount, Question, Webhook, Category, Format, Media, TicketGroup, EventSeries, EventTeam). The catalog_enumeration_result.json confirms 18 record types. Runtime D4 SoftPKClassifier will validate per-IO.

WriteCapability.notes: Full CRUD is available for Events (POST create, POST update), Ticket Classes (POST create, POST update, DELETE), Discounts (POST create, POST update), Venues (POST create, POST update), Webhooks (POST create, DELETE), Media (POST create/upload), Event Series (POST create, POST update). Read-only: Orders (GET only in public API), Attendees (GET only), Categories/Formats (GET only — system-managed). Update uses POST (not PATCH/PUT) on most Eventbrite endpoints. See WriteCapabilityNotes for per-object detail.
WriteCapability.writeCapabilityNotes: Events use POST to /events/ for create and POST to /events/{id}/ for update (note: update uses POST, not PATCH/PUT — Eventbrite convention). Ticket classes use POST to /events/{id}/ticket_classes/ for create and POST to /events/{id}/ticket_classes/{id}/ for update. Organizations, Attendees, Orders, Categories, Formats are read-only via the public API.

Configuration.ConcurrencyControlNotes: The Eventbrite API v3 spec defines no ETag, If-Match, If-Unmodified-Since, or version-number fields on any resource. The Waypoint mechanism (Eventbrite-API-Waypoint-Token header on POST/DELETE responses; echoed back on the next request for immediate consistency) is a consistency helper for rapid sequential writes, not a concurrency control mechanism. No optimistic concurrency headers are documented. Conflict resolution must use snapshot-3-way only.
Configuration.DeleteSemanticsNotes: Eventbrite API v3 DELETE operations (e.g. DELETE /webhooks/{webhook_id}/) are hard deletes with no tombstone or soft-delete/archive-flag mechanism documented in the spec. Event cancellation/deletion removes the event. No tombstone fields or separate deleted-records endpoints are documented. Orphaned records in the destination cannot be detected from the API alone without webhook subscription.
Configuration.DefaultSyncDirectionReasoning: Read-only (Pull) by default per policy. Eventbrite is the system of record for events, registrations, orders, and attendees; the connector reads those into the MJ entity store. Write-path (bidirectional) requires sandbox validation and clear organizational decisions before enabling against a live Eventbrite account. No ETag/version concurrency control means conflict resolution is snapshot-3-way only.
Configuration.DefaultConflictResolutionReasoning: No ETag or version field is available — MostRecent is not reliably safe. DestWins is the conservative default when bidirectional is eventually enabled, treating the MJ entity store as the destination.

ErrorResponseShape.schema: { error: string, error_description: string, status_code: number }
ErrorResponseShape.example: { "error": "VENUE_AND_ONLINE", "error_description": "You cannot both specify a venue and set online_event", "status_code": 400 }
ErrorResponseShape.notes: All errors return: (1) HTTP status code in 400-500 range, (2) JSON body with three fields: error (constant machine-readable string), error_description (human-readable explanation for developers), status_code (mirrors HTTP status for convenience). Common errors: 400 ACTION_NOT_PROCESSED, 400 ARGUMENTS_ERROR, 400 BAD_CONTINUATION_TOKEN, 400 BAD_PAGE, 400 BAD_REQUEST, 400 REQUEST_CONFLICT (also 409), 401 NOT_AUTH (not authorized), 403 NOT_PERMITTED, 404 NOT_FOUND, 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED, 409 REQUEST_CONFLICT, 429 HIT_RATE_LIMIT, 500 EXPANSION_FAILED.

Configuration.RateLimitModelNotes: Default rate limit: 2,000 calls per hour per token. Exceeding returns HTTP 429 with error code HIT_RATE_LIMIT. The spec documents this as the default; higher limits may be available through Eventbrite partner agreements. No documented daily limit or per-endpoint limits in the v3 spec. BatchMaxRequestCount=2000, BatchRequestWaitTime=3600 (seconds per hour).
Configuration.CustomObjectMarkerPatternNotes: Eventbrite API v3 does not expose custom object types. There is no customer-extensible object model or custom object creation endpoint. The object catalog is fixed (Events, Orders, Attendees, Venues, TicketClasses, Discounts, etc.). Per-tenant runtime customization is limited to custom Questions (per-event survey questions) whose answer values (answers per order/attendee) are runtime data — not schema-extension.
Configuration.CustomFieldMarkerPatternNotes: Eventbrite API v3 does not have a generic custom field mechanism. Event organizers can define Questions (GET/POST /events/{id}/questions/) which function as custom per-event survey fields. Question answers on Attendees and Orders are per-tenant runtime data (the answers field on Attendee records). These are NOT Declared as IOF rows — they are runtime data that varies per event and per organization, captured by the framework custom-column capture mechanism (full record pass-through → __mj_integration_CustomOverflow). Question definitions themselves (the Questions IO) are in-scope as a Declared IO since the endpoint is static.
Configuration.DiscoveryIsAuthoritativeNotes: No describe-all or schema endpoint exists in the Eventbrite API v3 that enumerates the full object catalog. The object catalog is fixed and credential-free (documented in apiary spec). Discovery at runtime enumerates organizational data (organizations, events, etc.) — not schema. Therefore DiscoveryIsAuthoritative stays false: absence from a runtime scan never means the object type is gone from the API, only that the current org has no data of that type.

OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.reason: Eventbrite exposes a Zapier integration and a Make (formerly Integromat) app for no-code automation. These are separate products with their own trigger/action models, not part of the Eventbrite REST API v3. Sync via these no-code platforms bypasses the direct REST API and is out of scope for this connector which targets the REST API v3 directly.

Webhook delivery (the inbound HTTP POST sent by Eventbrite to the registered endpoint_url when an event.created, order.placed, etc. action fires) is a push signal, not a REST API resource. It requires a publicly-reachable HTTPS endpoint to receive; it is not accessible via the REST API. Webhook subscription management (CRUD on /organizations/{org_id}/webhooks/) IS in scope. Webhook delivery ingestion is out of scope because it is architectural infrastructure (an inbound HTTP listener), not a sync pull stream.

This connector targets the Eventbrite REST API v3 for event management data (events, registrations, attendees, orders). It is intentionally scoped to Eventbrite-native data. ETL into a CRM (e.g. Salesforce Contacts from Attendees), AMS (e.g. member event history), or Data Warehouse (aggregate reporting) is an integration pattern that should be implemented at the EntityMap/field-mapping layer in MJ, not by expanding the scope of the Eventbrite connector itself to include destination-system writes.
